title: Evaluating inverse trig functions at exact values
problem: Find the exact value of each of the following in radians: (a) $\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, (b) $\cos^{-1}\!\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$, (c) $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$. (Each inverse trig function has a restricted range: $\sin^{-1}(x)$ maps to $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$, $\cos^{-1}(x)$ maps to $[0, \pi]$, and $\tan^{-1}(x)$ maps to $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.)

steps.working: Since $\cos\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and cosine is negative in the second quadrant, $\cos\!\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \cos\!\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, and $\dfrac{3\pi}{4} \in [0, \pi]$, so $\cos^{-1}\!\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

steps.instruction: Evaluate $\sin\!\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)$, noting $\frac{7\pi}{6}$ lies in the third quadrant ($\pi < \frac{7\pi}{6} < \frac{3\pi}{2}$).
Apply $\sin^{-1}$ to the result, recalling that $\sin^{-1}$ always returns a value in $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$.
steps.working: $$\sin^{-1}\!\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6}$$ since $-\dfrac{\pi}{6} \in \left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and $\sin\!\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$. The identity $\sin^{-1}(\sin(\theta)) = \theta$ does not apply here because $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ is outside $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.
